reason: Browser TVP-SV uses diagonal contemporaneous covariance and fixed state innovation variances. Mean-reverting or random-walk volatility and an explicit outlier mixture are available. Full time-varying triangular covariance with learned state scales adds thousands of latent states and requires multi-chain convergence assessment.
retained: Full triangular covariance, learned coefficient/volatility/impact state scales, optional outlier mixture, NUTS/HMC/ADVI; no named-paper prior replication is claimed.

reason: The bundled common panel is quarterly and revised, not a monthly release-vintage panel. Quarterly observations cannot responsibly be interpolated into monthly observations. Browser DFM uses a genuine state-space likelihood; the native mixed-frequency implementation takes an explicitly dated monthly panel and quarterly growth.
retained: Statsmodels DynamicFactorMQ with quarterly aggregation restrictions, EM and missing observations.

reason: PyTorch and pretrained Chronos checkpoints are not distributed in the pinned Pyodide runtime. Adding a separate tensor runtime and model weights would exceed the shared-runtime architecture and initial package budget. The browser trains real small RNN/LSTM/TCN/Transformer models; these are not called pretrained models.
retained: Actual CPU Chronos-T5-tiny inference with a required model commit revision and fixed random seed.

reason: The cited climate application requires observed local physical- and transition-risk covariates. No such replication dataset is bundled, and NFCI is not relabelled as a climate proxy. The supplied full function accepts observed climate covariates and unit identifiers.
retained: Pooled quantile regression with climate covariates and unit effects. This is a method illustration, not a causal or exact paper replication.

reason: The real 11-firm panel supports live pooled, Mean Group, hierarchical and collapsed difference/system GMM estimation. Eleven units do not justify reliable large-N overidentification or serial-correlation-test p-values; moment residuals and relevance are reported. The VARX network option imposes equal foreign-unit weights, not fabricated trade weights.
retained: Genuine one-step moment estimation and partial-pooling Gibbs sampling. No claim that GMM removes every short-panel or weak-instrument problem.

reason: DF–GLS and the known-break exercise display Monte Carlo critical values for a specified Gaussian null, sample size and lag order. The known-break exercise is explicitly Perron-style, not a reproduction of every innovation/additive-outlier case in Perron (1989). Multiple-break locations minimise trimmed global SSR; no conventional F p-value is attached to a searched break date.
retained: PP long-run variance correction, GLS detrending, known-break augmented regression, Chow test and global segmented regression.

reason: The direct-horizon DVAR estimates two conditional marginals using regularised distribution logits and a triangular factorisation. It differs from the cited three-variable empirical application. CDF interpolation stays on observed support; no parametric tail density, log score or structural policy interpretation is asserted.
retained: Direct multi-step joint distribution forecasts and changes in growth quantiles/CDFs under an explicit conditioning scenario.
